Eamon: The name of a particular colour of paint. He’s not black, he’s not grey and he’s not blue - he’s Eamon, and he pleasantly fills background space without tearing the room to pieces. Is he boring?...Mmm, a little bit.
Earl: Earl loves either gridiron, rugby or soccer, he lives for ten pin bowling with his pals every Friday night and he is a gifted hooligan, in general. He wears lots of rings.
Early: Early has clear head and he doesn’t talk shit. He may have had a tough start to life but it has made him tough and true at the finish.
East: Ignore the brooding good looks and the occasionally cool facade because East is a lovely fellow who simply isn't as outgoing as one might expect him to be. He approaches his career/careers like an old diesel engine which takes ages to get up to speed: in the beginning he stops and coughs and spits abit, but once his revs are up he's a fine specimen. (Note: he's much better off outdoors than in and he's not really the kinky type.)
Easton: A lot more volatile than he looks. If no one keeps an eye on Easton he’ll end up off the map. Give him something to do and encourage him in it. He ain’t someone who needs to spend oodles of time inside his own head.
Eckhart:
His name curls around itself like a content koala up in a tree. Ever seen one in the wild? You’ll be lucky to see one moving. At best you might see one munching on a gum leaf, but usually they seem to be asleep. They never appear to concern themselves with the future, they definitely don’t concern themselves with the past, and all they appear to deal with is the unfolding present moment, and where their substantive imagination takes them. 
I give you Eckhart.
Ed: Closely related to Malcolm, Ed is a huge log that you throw on the fire in the dead of winter. He is a massive awkward thing that takes a while to lumber into place but once he gets going he throws out enough steadying light, heat and humour to warm all but the biggest of rooms. (Serendipity is his close ally although he is a little lazy in bed.)
Eddie: Full of wisecracks and hair-brain schemes.
Eden: Eden is perfectly centred, he is innovative and he carries a glorious sense of fun. He’d make a good father.
Edgar: A nice thick piece of cheddar cheese. Pregnant women sometimes crave his company and he often forms the part of many-a-meal that might be described as ‘comfort food’.
Edgy: Cryptic crosswords and scrabble - I fucking doubt it. Edgy is too busy cave diving. Perhaps he’s ice climbing or snow boarding? Edgy is the sort of fellow who will host a party that is so loud and packed with people the entire house will need re-stumping afterwards.
Edison: If he were a chimpanzee, while the rest of his troop swung and hooted and hollered around him, being silly in the moment, Edison would hang pendulous by a single arm, contemplating whatever the equivalent of the chimpanzee money market is. Does that make him boring? Well, perhaps, but we all have a niche to fill.
Edmund:
As Walter’s younger cousin, Edmund says, “Yes dear”, “No dear”, “Sorry dear” and, “Okay dear”, so often that he sometimes says them in his sleep. 
Poor Edmund.
Edward: Edward always wears spectacles. As a leading diplomat in the foreign office he spends most of his time placating visiting V.I.Ps who are still offended by the behaviour of some of his embassy staff at the party that was held the night before.
Edwin: Edwin joined the Navy and became an officer - more for the white uniform than to actually go into battle. However he can only compute only one order at a time and he can’t swim freestyle for more than 35 metres before he starts to inhale water.
Egor:
Here's a tip: If you're the central umpire adjudicating a game of tennis in which Egor is playing and you make a call that he believes is wrong, you won't hear him yell and scream at you, oh no. But you might have to dodge his racquet currently flying at your head. (And it doesn’t matter if it's a Grand Slam event, or just a 'friendly' Sunday afternoon get-together with a few friends.)

PS- Don't take it personally.
Einar: His parents were Swedish politicians, which is one thing, but no one has any idea how to either spell or pronounce his name. The only thing we know for certain is that Einar rhymes with “When do you think your gonna’?”, and to that end he charges at life like a drunk village idiot in a bad mood. Get in his way and you’re basically fucked.
Eion: The more complex the game, the better. He's an academic who, like Bernard, has never once changed the oil in any car he has ever owned.
Eko: A cross between a gecko, a rainforest and an extroverted hairdresser, Eko and his Indonesian heritage are the perfect example of compassion, good grace and cheeky clean fun.
Elan: Elan drives a sports car with tan leather gloves, he wears a white or cream-coloured polo neck jumper that costs at least $800, even when it's not that cold, and he shaves his nuts at least as much as Marco.
Elfin:
(Said very quietly) Now, Elfin, if you can just come this way please and go and speak to those people through there. They'll be able to help you, okay?
(Postscript: Elfin moves to where he is supposed to go, to the room where mental assistance awaits for those who presume they are a character from a movie. We think he’s going to be fine. It might take a while though…)
Elian: Elian, it might be time to go and break some rules son. Just for the hell of it…
Elias:
Elias looks relaxed. He’s sitting next to his boss, the CEO, and he can feel his superior’s sudden rush of fear. What was supposed to be an initial, friendly discussion about a possible investment has been turned on its head. Clearly, what these three immaculately dressed visitors have in mind is a hostile takeover. 
The CEO is passed a piece of paper with a number written on it, and he sits there staring at it. Elias flicks a glance sideways and he can sense the fear amid his superior’s indecision. Immediately, Elias leans in to his colleague and suggests they have a quick word outside. 
Out in the foyer Elias whispers quietly, “Fuck those backstabbing mother fuckers. We’ve done too much. We’ve invested too much, and finally we’ve got this place working. We don’t need their money and you know it. Forget what the board thinks John. Let’s go back in there and you tell them to go and get fucked. And if you don’t I will.”
John smiles. He knows Elias is right. He’s always right…
Eligh: Deeper than you perceive, Eligh would make a wonderful crook because with a face as innocent as his, let alone his capacity to act very well, no one would ever suspect him.
Elijah: The Rattlesnake, which is to say what you see and hear is rarely the truth.
Eliot:
“Oh no,” Eliot’s wife says to their two kids, handing them the invite to the fancy dress party. “Have a look at this. But quick, I think that's your father in the driveway now.”
Her son reads the card and drops his head with a defeated sigh, while her daughter looks at her mother in a panic and says, “Oh Muuuuuum. Can we just not tell him this time? Pleeeeeeasssssssse? He gets so excited by these things he doesn't even sleep!” And amen to that, young Eliot.
Elliott: An upstanding man who doesn’t take things too seriously, and overall he’s excellent company. Aside from being highly intelligent, Elliott is also the name of a musical note that’s played on a flute by a man wearing tights.
Ellis: There's an American air force base named after him, which is fine by him. He's always liked a man in uniform.
Elon: It's a relaxing-sounding name, isn't it? Yet a little surprising at the same time too, which is why he's so good to have at sea - the last thing anyone needs in a confined space is an emotional idiot affecting the moral of the whole crew, plus he always keeps you thinking. Indeed, as the world's best racing-yacht tactician Elon is positioned perfectly up there near the helm right next to the skipper, so his directives can be taken up immediately. And chances are, if the skipper does what they're told with the resources available to them, victory will be assured. Nice work Elon.
Elroy: No, Elroy is never going to make the sacrifices needed to travel to faraway lands, set up a colony and start life afresh on the other side of the planet. He's quick-fix kind of guy. Friends come and go fast in his life because he's never in the same place twice.
Elton:
Bored at staring up at a black board for nine months and studying things he wasn't that fussed about, by the time exams began he was at the end of his tether, but, he walked into the exam room having studied his fair measure. He sat down, the clock began, 150 students opened their exam booklets and he did the same. Then, in a moment of clarity, quite slowly Elton closed his, took a breath and stood up.
“No. Fuck this. I’ve tried, but I’ve had enough.” Elton.
Elvis: When all the other parties have petered out on a Friday or Saturday night, everyone heads back to Elvis’s pad and to the one party that will ride it out to the dawn, and possibly the one after.
Elwood: "Well, howdy, y'all...... My names Elwood. I'm buddies with JD and I really like eatin' cake. Greeeaaaat big piles of cake.......!!! What do you like?...." Even labrador dogs are embarrassed by him.
Elwyn: Austerity measures? No, Elwyn is more into celebratory measures and techniques. Sure, he seems quiet and almost timid but not once you know him. Most of his humour runs far too deep for the average punter on the street.
Ely: Focus, is the key, son. FOCUS!
Emerson: As another one who is in love with stationary, Emerson rarely gets his hands dirty and is destined for a life and a career indoors. Does he exercise or dance? Let's hope so…
Emery: Emery is the captain of most of the school’s sports teams. As a natural (yet non-egotistical) leader, he is sought out for opinion and counsel both on and off the field, and he stands up for his team mates, which is why they adore him. But it can be a double-edged sword. Emery is made of rather strict moral fibre, you see, and whoa-betide any of his chargers who he discovers taking ecstasy the week before the grand final. No matter how good they are and no matter how badly he thinks the team needs them, such an act would result in instant dismissal. As you can imagine, the ladies simply adore him as well.
Emil: As a quiet and gentle-mannered man who has a particular kind of relationship with both the stars and some of the four-legged creatures which surround us, Emil should think about getting away from city life where he is often led down sleazy and unhealthy paths. He should think about becoming a goat herder…(It’d do you good, Emil.)
Emile: As girl called Gabriela in a past life, Emile is one cool cat. True, and just like Coco, actually, he’s barely ever lifted a shovel but so what? Keep on slidin’ Emile, keep on slidin’…
Emilio: Like the good-looking wake of a luxury yacht, Emilio trails just behind the chaos with something of a smile, knowing all the hard work has been done by someone else, up ahead. And that's okay. The only trade off is that when a situation gets particularly precarious, confronting or downright ugly, there's a chance he'll take his easy smile and his gentle joie de vivre around the corner and vanish altogether.
Emmanuel: Come on rock star, stop talking it up and show us what you've got!
Emmerson:
Like is his twin brother with the one m, Emmerson is a modern, technologically-fluent man who doesn’t know the first thing about dirt, worms and permaculture. And that’s okay. In the new era of clean energy, stain-free sheets and well-tended old-growth forests, we’ll need Emmerson in admin to make sure all the apps holding the modern world together are functioning smoothly. 
(Note: If Emmerson is born in South or Central America, Spain or Portugal, we have no fucking idea what he’s up to. He could drive a garbage truck for all we know, although whatever he's doing he’d be funny to sit next to.)
Emmett: In a past life Emmett hunted alligators in the Florida everglades like you see on one of those stupid bloody television shows. Today in this life he still answers most questions with one syllable if possible, but he’s a whole lot friendlier and smarter, and his personal hygiene has improved through the roof. Peace out Emmett.
Ennio: Have you ever noticed how some people just seem to have more time than others? It's weird. Ennio is the sort of fellow who doesn’t need to mediate because he unwittingly mediates all the time, just by breathing in and out, deeply and slowly. He'd make a gifted free diver and probably break all sorts of records, and here on land it endears him with a wonderful sense of calm which is wholly infectious. What's he doing these days? Who cares. He's happy and he's at peace, and so are those around him. Amen to that, young Ennio.
Enrique: In Spain he might as well be called Shane – who knows – but here, he’s a potent ball of energy that, like several of his peers, lives for the sight of girls’ knickers. And he generally gets to see plenty.
Enzo:
Option A: Oh look, go and watch the movie The Big Blue. It'll save everyone time.

Option B: A large male poodle who knows his photo is being taken, and who will pose accordingly. In that regard he is identical to his human brother.
Eric: Eric is a light-hearted Goat and one of the Gifted Ones in that he is the luckiest being in the entire Kingdom. Outstanding effort, Eric. (Okay, okay, so some Erics are incredibly lazy and make useless husbands, not that he’s ever aware of that.)
Erich: As a palaeontologist of some note, Erich is very excited by shovels and brushes, not to mention canvas sock protectors.
Erik: The academic with a very dry sense of humour. He's often so engrossed in his studies/projects that if you passed him in the corridor and said hello he'd barely notice you were there, let alone respond. Don't take it personally.
Erin: Another Arts student. Erin wears $420 shirts and aches to resemble one of those dopy male models in a magazine ad for Christ-knows-what.
Ernan: What Ernan would never do is allow any of the machines that he owns to fall into a state of disrepair. Car, truck, lawn mower or chainsaw, and especially the electric winch that he built himself to haul buckets of water up from the dam, Ernan keeps a close eye on all his gadgets. I shudder to think what he gets up to in bed.
Ernest: The name of an old country homestead that sits on a rich pastoralist’s property. Quiet, calm and cool in the heat of the summer, he battens down the hatches in winter and hibernates.
Ernesto: Ernesto has charisma, and he has no issues around declaring bankruptcy. If things are good then great, he’ll live large and hold up a candle to the good times and he’ll foot the bill. But at the first sign of an inevitable storm he’s out the back door as quick as a heated tomcat and fuck the consequences about angry creditors who have been left in the lurch. No storm = no trouble. His personal life is therefore more dramatic than most.
Ernie: Yeah, yeah, he’s heard the Benny Hill jokes. Forget all that for a tic. Ernie is loving and compassionate, and sure, he’ll never fully grow up, but perhaps that means he ism already because aren’t highly evolved souls the best at playing in this moment?
Errin: Perhaps we need to ship Errin off to Palestine, then Syria, then Afghanistan, then Chechnya, then basically anywhere large groups of people are in conflict? You see, Errin is a peaceful man who exudes calm, and who encourages one to contemplate their inner-turmoils. Forgiveness: he accidentally promotes this without even meaning to. Weird, eh? But don’t presume by all this that he represents a serious man. He's not, he's just young at heart.
Errol: A Fiat Bambino 500 motorcar. Forget Herbie the Clint, Errol has style and panache, and he makes others laugh by simply looking at him.
Erwin: Erwin is a peculiar man. Because he is supremely dogmatic he is well-suited to his profession of an investigative reporter. He's been threatened with the sack so often from the chief editor that it doesn't even register anymore. Like a tenacious Jack Russell with his eye on the truth, Erwin will persist, and ask, and probe until he finds the REAL STORY. And he's great at feigning igronance if he's over-spent his budget.
Essex:
Oh dear, once again we find a set of parents who’s own parents required a decent education. What is one to do? Anyway, here is Essex, a young man (and grandson) named-so in the hope he will be propelled into a cool and unique setting (personality) and where fame and fortune await. 

(Private Message from Management to Essex: Essex, brother, beware the fools in your midst. Their sense of self-worth is not great, and this is a potential vacuum which, without an eye to the outside greater world, might suck you down with it. You with me? …..good. So, have some fun then get out. It’s a big, wonderful world and you will do well in and upon it. Amen.)
ET: E.T simply can't belieeeeeeeve how good he looks. And he's a happy man.
Ethan: “Eee – than” rhymes with “Not – fair”. As a serious young man who lacks the ability to grow any kind of facial hair, the only avenue for Ethan to look older or serious, therefore, is to frown constantly. But dont let that dissuade you. Ethan is a lovely, gentle fellow.
Ethen: Ethen has slightly less time to waste than his twin brother, Ethan, which means he gets to places faster in lieu of spending less time thinking about how and where he is going. Still, there is some uncertainty about where he really wants to be and why. Is this why he looks quite serious, usually?
Etienne: Etienne wears scarves in his hair and a myriad of thin, multi-coloured leather bracelets on his wrist. Travelled, yes, French, probably, either in this life or a recent past one, and he wields a massive depth of interest in those who have experienced a different life history to his, which, let’s face it, is most people. Etienne isn’t a hard man, but he tries hard at being loving and optimistic. That makes him tough enough in anyone’s language. Etienne, the feathers in your hair look ridiculous but we don’t care. We’re just glad you're around.
Euan: Like a fine aged wine, Euan is in for the long haul. He takes no shortcuts and he’s very much about the journey. He does what he says, he’s mild-mannered and he is the one of the most patient people you will ever meet.
Eugene: For an unusual name Eugene is just a normal sort of bloke, and a nice one. (Note: The thing about Eugene is that, though his name begins oddly, it quite quickly becomes an unexpectedly smooth ride over rolling green hills.)
Ev: Ev is one of the good guys. He’s open in dealings, he’s friendly in company, he enjoys kids and strangers and he helps out. Barely a bad word ever gets said about him, and rightly so.
Evan: It doesn’t happen much these days because the world’s gone to CDs and beyond but once upon a time vinyl records were all the rage and sometimes they received scratches, and every time the needle ran over one it would skip. “Evan…Evan…Evan..,” the speakers would blurt, and you’d drop your head at another album destroyed. (Yes, Evan is hyper-organised and no one wishes that he wasn’t. Amen.)
Everard: Boy, was he barked at a lot. Let’s hope he gets “Ev” or “Evo”, otherwise he’s going to plod along in the guise of a rather staid, conservative and ostensibly boring individual.
Everest: Well, at least they didn't call you K2. That'd be flat out silly now, wouldn't it? As it happens, Everest isn't the mountain we were led to believe, but he's a decent person. And yes, once again we see parents drunk in front of an atlas trying to name a child - what do you do?
Evo: A pulsating individual who has done it all. A huge smile on his face is always a good start, but Evo is traipsing through life as if charging through virgin jungle with a machete, and he’s had a few of those too. Was he a stripper for a while or am I making that up? Last I heard he was setting up a surfing backpackers in Ecuador, but that was a while back. Perhaps they made a TV show about him? Is he still alive?….
Ewan: You can’t help but contort the inside of your throat to say it, but somehow he manages to pull-off a great comeback. Regardless of that, Ewan is a nice guy and a skilled carpenter who is as good with his hands as he is with his repartee.
Exavier: Exavier is too polite to be particularly manly. But, he did well at school and he’ll probably do well at university if he attends. He was never going to be a plumber. He's not quick witted enough for a start.
Eyre:
Option A: The gifted yoga Instructor who spends a fortune on hemp clothing. 


Option B: Property Developer who is another Quiet Achiever. No one knows how much money he has, where he spends his nights or what his deeper desires are. Some potential advise Eyre: don't believe all the hype about buying a house or houses. I mean, that's fine and dandy if you want to spend all your time accruing wealth, but flat, calm, safe and satisfying ground can be found anywhere your heart is having its desires met. Indeed, chaos is good for the soul.
Ezekial: Nice guy, but a little lost in the adult world most of the time.
Ezekiel:
Ezekiel is the name of a B-52 nuclear bomber in the US air force. And that’s great. Except one day he’s on a training mission with real nukes on board, and that’s okay too, until a computer malfunction instructs his crew to divert him to Moscow and drop their payload. Poor Ezekiel. It’s not even his fault, really. All incoming radio contact is immediately scrambled, however, and if we don’t stop him, the retaliatory strikes from Russia effectively mean we’re all fucked. 
The moral to the story? Can someone just keep an eye on this young man for us, from time to time?….thanks.
Ezra: His hair is curly because he is sufficiently electrifying, hence I would advise not getting too close to him if there’s a lightning storm overhead, and you are either wet or standing on some kind of metal. He’s a great fire twirler.
